How Kubernetes, helm and these images behave: A StatefulSet with updateStrategy RollingUpdate replaces its pods one at a time from the highest ordinal, deleting each old pod before it creates its replacement (there is no surge); with partition N, pods with an ordinal below N keep the old version; with OnDelete no pod is replaced until someone deletes it. A replacement pod mounts the same PVCs from volumeClaimTemplates. A pod's emptyDir volumes and its container filesystem are deleted together with the pod; only data on a PersistentVolume outlives it. When a PVC is deleted, its PersistentVolume and the data on it are deleted if the reclaimPolicy is Delete; with Retain the volume and its directory stay on the node (Released). Deleting a StatefulSet or scaling it down keeps the PVCs created from its volumeClaimTemplates, unless its persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy says Delete for that case (whenDeleted or whenScaled). A StatefulSet pod that is deleted is recreated with the same name and the same PVC name; if that PVC is gone, a new empty one is created. The postgres image applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD only when it initializes an empty data directory; a data directory that already holds a database keeps its users, passwords and pg_hba.conf. An empty data directory is initialized as a new, empty database. A Service sends connections only to ready pods whose labels match every key of its selector, on its targetPort (a number, or the name of a container port of those pods); with no such pod, or nothing listening there, connections fail. A Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, and a container hostPort, can be reached from outside the cluster on the node's address; a ClusterIP Service only from inside the cluster. Once a NetworkPolicy selects a pod, the pod accepts only the ingress that its policies allow; a pod selected by no policy accepts traffic from every namespace. A namespaceSelector {} matches every namespace. helm upgrade applies the chart rendered with only the values given in that command (the previous release's values are not reused, except when the command gives no values at all, or an empty values file, in which case helm reuses them); the rendered objects listed are what gets applied, and objects the new rendering no longer contains are deleted. helm uninstall deletes the release's objects but not the PVCs created from a StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplates. A PodDisruptionBudget limits evictions (node drains); it does not slow down or block a rollout.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
